comment: The ref kinds and EVENTS this factory declares BEYOND the instrument's core set. A ref is a typed pointer from a row to another object; the core kinds are row, subject, commit, session, rework. Core events are genesis, intake, claim, dispatch, close, score, ruling, run. Declare here when this factory carries a kind or an event the core vocabulary lacks -- e.g. inferhub-watch's 'ack' event (8 rows) belongs in ITS OWN copy of this file, which is how a member's own vocabulary becomes lawful without forking tools/ledger.py. The value of a member's object stays opaque to the tool: a miidas contour such as zamer/01 travels as a ref whose KIND is declared here. A declaration ADDS; it never removes or redefines a core entry. THIS factory declares 'release' (#210, ruling n=1577) -- the claim-release transition, so a claim that was WITHDRAWN is representable rather than reading as in-flight forever. A release row carries the released claim's own row number as a ref of kind 'row' plus a stated reason; a release naming no claim is refused at the write path, because it would be indistinguishable from an intake. Declared HERE and NOT added to the core tuple: a member that never withdraws a claim carries no dead vocabulary, and the transition promotes to the core set when a second factory needs it. THIS factory ALSO declares 'conversion' (#67, ruling n=1599) -- the score-regression conversion: its row names the artifact it answered as `converted_from=evidence/scores/<date>.md` in its canonical run, and a conversion naming no artifact is refused at the write path, because an unattributable conversion can never be joined to the regression it was meant to answer. THIS factory ALSO declares 'park' and 'unpark' (#535, ruling n=4007) -- the block-on-owner transition, so a subject's parked state is a TRANSITION read in row order rather than a `park:owner:qN` string grepped out of free prose. A `park` row carries the register question as a ref of the DECLARED kind 'question' and is REFUSED at the write path when it names none; an `unpark` row carries the park row it supersedes as a ref of kind 'row' plus a stated reason, and both are refused when absent. The kind 'question' is declared HERE for the same reason: the core kinds name rows, subjects, commits, sessions and rework, and a register question is none of those. A token scan could not answer the question the transition answers -- n=3339 names a park in the prose of the row that ENDED it, and n=2884 names three parks in a ruling whose subject is a fourth unit. THIS factory ALSO declares 'board' (#580, ruling n=4448) -- the tracker item a `conversion` row ROUTED its round into. Section 5.4 item 4 of the measurement procedure made routing the conversion's PRECONDITION and supplied no field for it, so a row could declare `routed` while naming nothing; the ref is that field, and the leg resolves it against the board. A TYPED ref was chosen over a `routed_to=#<n>` prose token on the `park:owner:qN` lesson exactly (n=3339, n=2884): a string grepped out of free prose is answered by the wrong row, while a ref of a declared kind is refused at the write path when it is absent or malformed -- and it cannot share a kind with `subject`, which already names the survey unit on the same event.
